pathway.title: Sba Communications Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Business quality is the main support: revenue is contracted, recurring and high-margin, but its domestic leg is shrinking. Site leasing produced 98.3% of segment operating profit in nine months 2026, tenant leases run 5 to 15 years with annual escalators, the domestic segment margin was 84.24% and the international 70.42%, and about 71% of towers sit on owned or long-dated land. Against that, domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.14% as Sprint, EchoStar and other leases were not renewed, and three U.S. carriers supply 66.5% of revenue, so a further carrier event would reach cash flow quickly. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12

Leverage is high and has not fallen through debt reduction. Net debt was 6.45x adjusted EBITDA and 7.39x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 6.61x and 7.73x at the end of 2025, and debt principal ended the nine months USD 15.25 million higher; counting the escrow held for the January 2025 repayment, end-2024 adjusted leverage was 6.46x, so leverage has been roughly flat near 6.5x for two years. Pro forma for the purchase of 69 sites expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, with no day stated, net leverage is 7.40x on reported EBITDA; the pro forma figure on adjusted EBITDA, for the dividend payable on 2026-12-10 and for the Peru sale is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 15; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Earnings momentum is flat and turned negative in the third quarter, so deleveraging cannot rely on EBITDA growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.11% over FY2025 on a last-twelve-months basis, was flat at constant currency in nine months 2026 and fell 1.9% at constant currency in the third quarter, because lower domestic and site development profit offset international growth. The adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue slipped to 67.78% from 70.69% in FY2024. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2

Free cash flow is solid but fully distributed. Operating cash flow after capital expenditure is 54.40% of adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest alone taking 24.60%, and dividends plus buybacks absorbed 98.49% of that free cash flow in the last twelve months, up from 56.40% in FY2024 and 91.59% in FY2025. The dividend alone is 49.19% of free cash flow, so buybacks are the discretionary half and the main lever. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C4

Interest cost will reset upward as low-coupon debt matures. The debt outstanding carries a weighted average coupon of 3.94%, adjusted EBITDA covers run-rate coupon interest 3.78x against 4.07x on cash interest paid, and the three maturities due within twelve months, the 2021-1C Tower Securities, the 2020 Senior Notes and the 2021-2C Tower Securities, all carry coupons below 4%. Replacing them at the July 2026 notes' coupon would take cover to about 3.22x, an assumption-based estimate that holds adjusted EBITDA flat. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C7

Liquidity is adequate for contractual maturities but depends on market access for the anticipated dates. Cash plus the undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver covers 194.50% of the USD 1,500 million of principal with a final maturity inside twelve months, but only 81.95% of the USD 3,560 million that includes the two Tower Securities tranches with anticipated repayment dates in that window; the revolver also backs the commercial paper program, so the two are not additive, and letters of credit are not stated. A tranche not repaid on its date traps cash flow from its towers and steps its interest up by at least 5 percentage points, so the dates behave like maturities for planning even though the legal maturities are decades away. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 19 and 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 132–133; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C9

Financial policy is acceptable but not conservative, and structure concentrates secured debt in one pool. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, but management ranks acquisitions and new towers, then buybacks, then dividend growth, and the nine-month record put payouts ahead of debt reduction; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium. The debt the filings state as secured fell to 49.90% of principal from 76.85% at the 2025 year end and sits in a non-recourse pool covering 19.01% of towers; reported covenant ratios and the pool's coverage ratio are not printed, so headroom is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 18 and 52; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13

runs.text: The strengths, in rank order, are these. The contracted, high-margin site leasing base is first: it produced 98.3% of segment operating profit, with margins of 84.24% in the U.S. and 70.42% abroad, and its recurring rent covers fixed charges and keeps cash interest at 24.60% of adjusted EBITDA. Demonstrated capital-markets access is second: USD 3,500 million of unsecured notes in July 2026, an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver and a commercial paper program give refinancing a path that does not depend on the securitisation market alone. Third is a fixed-rate, laddered debt stack with a low weighted average coupon of 3.94%, which holds near-term interest cost down until the older tranches reset. Fourth is control of the land: about 71% of towers sit on owned, perpetual or long-dated land interests with a 35-year average remaining life. Fifth is discretion: no sponsor is identified and the board can cut buybacks, which are about the size of the dividend, at its sole discretion. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C13

The weaknesses, in rank order, are these. Leverage comes first: net debt is 6.45x adjusted EBITDA and 7.39x reported EBITDA (7.40x on reported EBITDA pro forma for the 69-site purchase; other post-balance-sheet effects not established) with principal flat, so creditors carry the same leverage as two years ago. Second, payouts absorb 98.49% of free cash flow, leaving nothing for debt reduction. Third, the near-term maturity concentration: USD 3,560 million of principal falls at anticipated dates within twelve months against liquidity that covers 81.95%. Fourth, customer concentration and churn: three carriers supply 66.5% of revenue, EchoStar has defaulted, and guided 2026 churn is about 6.61% to 6.81% of FY2025 site leasing revenue. Fifth, the interest reset against flat earnings: adjusted EBITDA was flat at constant currency in nine months 2026 and fell in the third quarter while cover on run-rate coupons is 3.78x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 31 and 45; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C12

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction of 2026 is the 2026-07-23 refinancing. The company issued USD 3,500 million of unsecured senior notes under its automatic shelf registration in three tranches (USD 1,350 million due January 2030, USD 1,350 million due July 2031 and USD 800 million due July 2033), terminated its prior senior credit agreement and entered a new unsecured agreement with the parent as borrower that provides a USD 2,500 million revolving facility maturing 2031-07-23. Net proceeds repaid the revolver (USD 1.0 billion) and the 2024 Term Loan (USD 2.2 billion) and funded general corporate purposes; USD 16.1 million of deferred financing fees and USD 4.0 million of discount were expensed. The new agreement carries a total net leverage ceiling of 7.50x (up to 8.00x for four quarters after qualified acquisitions) and a senior secured leverage ceiling of 3.50x, and on 2026-09-25 the company added a USD 2,500 million commercial paper program backed by the revolver, with nothing drawn at the filing date. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 49–52; calculation C11

The secured debt that remains is the Tower Securities, a non-recourse mortgage loan to a group of subsidiary borrowers backed by 8,603 towers at 2026-09-30 (9,498 at 2025-12-31). The 2020-1C Tower Securities of USD 750 million were repaid on 2026-01-09 with revolver borrowings, and the USD 1,165 million 2021-1C Tower Securities have an anticipated repayment date of 2026-11-09, which the company says it expects to refinance; the 2021-2C Tower Securities follow on 2027-04-09. If an anticipated repayment date is missed, cash flow from the pledged towers is trapped and the interest rate steps up, so the date is a hard test of market access rather than a legal maturity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 131–133; calculation C7

Acquisitions have shifted from a large Central America purchase to small and opportunistic buying. The 2024 purchase agreement with Millicom for over 7,000 sites at about USD 975.0 million in cash closed during 2025 and brought 7,110 towers, a seven-year right to build up to 2,500 sites and 15-year lease-back agreements; total 2025 tower acquisitions cost USD 1,009.935 million. In nine months 2026 the company bought 23 towers and the rights to the land under about 3,900 Guatemala sites (USD 109.0 million), spent USD 204.677 million in all on acquisitions, and has 69 further sites for USD 17.9 million expected to close in the fourth quarter. Contingent consideration of up to USD 62.3 million is not recorded. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 5 and 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 47

Disposals and shareholder actions complete the picture. The company completed the Philippines sale on 2025-01-10, sold the Philippines and Colombia towers and substantially all of its Canada operations in 2025 for USD 330.4 million in total with a USD 208.4 million gain, sold all Chile and Ecuador towers in the third quarter of 2026 for USD 134.2 million, and agreed on 2026-09-10 to sell its Peru towers, with USD 77.6 million of assets held for sale. The board authorised a USD 1,500 million repurchase plan on 2025-04-27, of which USD 822.884 million remained at 2026-09-30, and a joint venture partner has given notice of its put to sell its interest, expected to close in the fourth quarter subject to regulatory approval. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 54 and 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 26 and 60

fields.value: Leverage has eased less than the headline suggests. fields.value: Reported EBITDA sits below the issuer's adjusted measure because the issuer adds back impairment and decommissioning costs, acquisition costs and non-cash compensation. In FY2025 impairment and decommissioning costs rose to USD 184.165 million from USD 107.925 million, which pulled reported EBITDA down to USD 1,635.071 million from USD 1,705.28 million while adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,912.104 million from USD 1,894.345 million. FY2025 net income of USD 1,054.456 million was lifted by a USD 208.399 million gain on sale of assets and a USD 119.925 million currency gain on intercompany loans, both outside EBITDA, so earnings quality is better judged through EBITDA and cash flow than through net income. The contrary view is that most impairment is non-cash (USD 174.085 million in FY2025), so adjusted EBITDA may describe cash earnings better; recurring impairment at this level would favour the reported measure.

fields.value: The interest burden is rising faster than earnings. Cash paid for interest increased from USD 395.112 million in FY2024 to USD 467.404 million in FY2025 and USD 475.532 million in the last twelve months, so cover on adjusted EBITDA slipped from 4.79x to 4.07x and on reported EBITDA stands at 3.55x. The 2026 senior notes carry a blended coupon of 5.113%, against 1.631% on the 2021-1C Tower Securities the issuer expects to refinance, so that refinancing would add to interest cost. Operating cash flow of USD 1,298.132 million in the last twelve months funded capital expenditure of USD 246.325 million and left free cash flow of USD 1,051.807 million, which dividends of USD 517.343 million and buybacks of USD 518.552 million absorbed almost entirely; acquisitions and debt repayment therefore depended on asset sale proceeds and new borrowing.

fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 2,917.532 million, made of cash of USD 417.532 million and the undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver, which also backs the commercial paper program. That is less than the USD 3,557.467 million of debt classified as current: the 2021-1C Tower Securities at their anticipated date of 2026-11-09, the 2020 Senior Notes due 2027-02-15 and the 2021-2C Tower Securities at 2027-04-09. The issuer says cash, facility availability and operating cash flow will cover debt service and final maturities over the next twelve months and anticipates refinancing the 2021-1C tranche. The strongest support is the market access shown by USD 3,500 million of unsecured senior notes issued in July 2026 and described as investment grade; the view would worsen if the 2021-1C tranche is not refinanced on or soon after its date, which the filings do not resolve, or if distributions continue at the current pace while 2027 maturities are drawn on the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance analysis for Sba Communications Corp (issuer sbac-1034054), as of 2026-11-18, on the Full credit assessment pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and capital allocation behaviour, and the 2024 to 2026 transaction and new debt history of the consolidated group, from five SEC filings; no sponsor, executed legal documents, ratings or market prices were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is neutral to modestly supportive: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and the articles generally cap any holder at 9.8%, but shareholder payouts absorb most free cash flow, so creditors rely on refinancing access and asset sales rather than retained cash for deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration and domestic churn are the larger risks. Three U.S. carriers supplied 66.5% of FY2025 revenue, domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.14% in nine months 2026, and dividends and buybacks took 86.54% of operating cash flow after capital expenditure. The July 2026 sale of USD 3,500 million of unsecured notes eased near-term refinancing risk, but the outcome for the 2021-1C Tower Securities due on 2026-11-09 and the proxy statement are not seen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control risk is low because the filings identify no sponsor or controlling holder, the board alone decides dividends and repurchases, and the articles generally bar any holder above 9.8%. That removes the sponsor-extraction and leveraged-buyout event risks that usually dominate high-yield governance, though holder-level ownership is untested because the proxy statement is not supplied. We rate sponsor and governance risk Medium rather than Low, because the payout policy and the unseen debt documents offset the clean control picture.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business model is a durable landlord franchise, but its domestic leg is shrinking. Site leasing produced 98.3% of segment operating profit in nine months 2026, on contracts with annual escalators; yet domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.14% as Sprint, EchoStar and other leases were not renewed, while international site leasing revenue rose 18.5% at constant currency, mainly from acquired and newly built towers. Management expects 2026 churn of USD 133.0 million to USD 136.0 million in the U.S. and USD 37.0 million to USD 39.0 million abroad, so net growth now leans on international acquisitions and tenancy rather than on U.S. rent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is the largest operating risk and one counterparty has already failed to pay. T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon together supplied 66.5% of FY2025 revenue and 87.8% of domestic site leasing revenue, and T-Mobile and Verizon supplied 96.1% of site development revenue. EchoStar defaulted on its payment obligations in December 2025 and the default continued into 2026, with expected churn of USD 56.0 million in 2026; the company says the default has not had and is not expected to have a material adverse effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder payouts, not sponsor extraction, are the governance leakage to watch. Dividends and buybacks took 86.54% of the cash that operating cash flow left after capital expenditure in nine months 2026, and 91.59% in FY2025, while debt principal ended the nine months USD 15.25 million higher. Management ranks acquisitions and new towers first, buybacks second and dividend growth third, and says debt repayment can be an accretive use of cash when rates are high; the nine-month record shows the ranking in practice put payouts ahead of debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C8; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The July 2026 refinancing improved maturity and security profile but changed the covenant yardstick. The USD 3,500 million of notes and the new USD 2,500 million revolver are unsecured, and they replaced a secured term loan and a drawn revolver, so the debt the filings state as secured fell to 49.90% of principal from 76.85% at the 2025 year end, all of it now in the Tower Securities. The leverage test moved to 7.50x on a consolidated basis from 6.5x on the old borrower group, so the earlier headroom cannot be carried over, and whether any subsidiary guarantees the new notes is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Portfolio pruning narrows the footprint while Central America and Brazil gain weight. The company sold its Philippines, Colombia and substantially all Canada operations in 2025, sold its Chile and Ecuador towers in the third quarter of 2026 for USD 134.2 million, and agreed to sell Peru, leaving about 10 of 12 international markets by our count. Brazil produced 14.1% of site leasing revenue and Guatemala holds about 10% of towers after the Millicom purchase, so single-country exposure rises as the tail of small markets is cut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring but not governance diligence. The auditor's FY2025 opinion says the statements present fairly in all material respects, its opinion on internal control is unqualified and officers found disclosure controls effective at 2026-09-30, yet board independence, related-party dealings and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and a director's trading arrangement adopted on 2026-06-18 was omitted from the second-quarter report and disclosed in the third.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a merely neutral-to-modest governance view is that the payouts are funded from operating cash flow rather than borrowing, the board refinanced into unsecured notes that the company describes as investment grade, with an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver, and the 9.8% ownership cap leaves no single holder positioned to direct a leveraged distribution. The company also describes debt repayment as potentially accretive, and no related-party fee, sponsor payment or dividend recapitalisation is disclosed in the supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would strengthen if the next filings show debt principal falling while payouts stay at the current rate, if the 2021-1C Tower Securities due on 2026-11-09 are refinanced on time, and if the proxy statement shows no holder near the cap. It would weaken if buybacks are funded by revolver or commercial paper borrowings, if payouts exceed operating cash flow after capital expenditure, if a further customer fails after EchoStar, or if the executed notes and credit agreement show wide restricted-payment capacity that the filings only describe as customary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ownership and control conclusion rests on the articles' 9.8% cap and on the absence of any named holder in the supplied text; holder-level ownership, board independence and related-party items are only in the 2026 proxy statement, so a holder near the cap or an interested director could exist unseen and would weaken the low control-risk view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ranking and structure conclusion uses the filings' summaries of the notes, the revolver and the mortgage loan; the executed indentures and credit agreement are absent, so guarantors of the 2026 notes, restricted-payment capacity and the security of the 2020 and 2021 notes are not established and the 49.90% secured share could be understated or overstated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The capital allocation conclusion compares payouts with operating cash flow after capital expenditure, but the filings do not tie the third-quarter buybacks to a funding source, so whether they were paid from the July borrowing proceeds or from cash flow is not established and the payouts-first reading could be too harsh or too mild.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The customer concentration conclusion uses revenue shares only; lease expiry dates, termination rights and the EchoStar receivable are not stated, so the pace at which concentration could turn into further churn is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The disposal and acquisition conclusions stop at 2026-11-05: the consideration for Peru, the price for the joint venture partner's put and the use of disposal proceeds are not stated, so the direction of the portfolio change is clear but its cash effect is not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction of 2026 is the 2026-07-23 refinancing. The company issued USD 3,500 million of unsecured senior notes under its automatic shelf registration in three tranches (USD 1,350 million due January 2030, USD 1,350 million due July 2031 and USD 800 million due July 2033), terminated its prior senior credit agreement and entered a new unsecured agreement with the parent as borrower that provides a USD 2,500 million revolving facility maturing 2031-07-23. Net proceeds repaid the revolver (USD 1.0 billion) and the 2024 Term Loan (USD 2.2 billion) and funded general corporate purposes; USD 16.1 million of deferred financing fees and USD 4.0 million of discount were expensed. The new agreement carries a total net leverage ceiling of 7.50x (up to 8.00x for four quarters after qualified acquisitions) and a senior secured leverage ceiling of 3.50x, and on 2026-09-25 the company added a USD 2,500 million commercial paper program backed by the revolver, with nothing drawn at the filing date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The secured debt that remains is the Tower Securities, a non-recourse mortgage loan to a group of subsidiary borrowers backed by 8,603 towers at 2026-09-30 (9,498 at 2025-12-31). The 2020-1C Tower Securities of USD 750 million were repaid on 2026-01-09 with revolver borrowings, and the USD 1,165 million 2021-1C Tower Securities have an anticipated repayment date of 2026-11-09, which the company says it expects to refinance; the 2021-2C Tower Securities follow on 2027-04-09. If an anticipated repayment date is missed, cash flow from the pledged towers is trapped and the interest rate steps up, so the date is a hard test of market access rather than a legal maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions have shifted from a large Central America purchase to small and opportunistic buying. The 2024 purchase agreement with Millicom for over 7,000 sites at about USD 975.0 million in cash closed during 2025 and brought 7,110 towers, a seven-year right to build up to 2,500 sites and 15-year lease-back agreements; total 2025 tower acquisitions cost USD 1,009.935 million. In nine months 2026 the company bought 23 towers and the rights to the land under about 3,900 Guatemala sites (USD 109.0 million), spent USD 204.677 million in all on acquisitions, and has 69 further sites for USD 17.9 million expected to close in the fourth quarter. Contingent consideration of up to USD 62.3 million is not recorded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disposals and shareholder actions complete the picture. The company completed the Philippines sale on 2025-01-10, sold the Philippines and Colombia towers and substantially all of its Canada operations in 2025 for USD 330.4 million in total with a USD 208.4 million gain, sold all Chile and Ecuador towers in the third quarter of 2026 for USD 134.2 million, and agreed on 2026-09-10 to sell its Peru towers, with USD 77.6 million of assets held for sale. The board authorised a USD 1,500 million repurchase plan on 2025-04-27, of which USD 822.884 million remained at 2026-09-30, and a joint venture partner has given notice of its put to sell its interest, expected to close in the fourth quarter subject to regulatory approval.

fields.value: Fundamental credit analysis for Sba Communications Corp (issuer sbac-1034054), as of 2026-11-18, on the Full credit assessment pathway. Scope is the consolidated group's business and financial profile, liquidity and refinancing capacity, a qualitative downside case and monitoring triggers, built on the financial foundation and the business and governance facts already established; no ratings, executed legal documents, market prices or sponsor were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit is adequate: a high-margin, contract-backed tower portfolio and demonstrated bond-market access support creditors, but high leverage and payouts that absorb 98.49% of free cash flow leave refinancing of near-term maturities as the decisive risk.

Liquidity covers 81.95% of the USD 3,560 million of principal due within twelve months at the Tower Securities' anticipated dates, and 96.97% with a year of free cash flow after dividends, so continued market access is needed even if buybacks stop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business quality is the main support: revenue is contracted, recurring and high-margin, but its domestic leg is shrinking. Site leasing produced 98.3% of segment operating profit in nine months 2026, tenant leases run 5 to 15 years with annual escalators, the domestic segment margin was 84.24% and the international 70.42%, and about 71% of towers sit on owned or long-dated land. Against that, domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.14% as Sprint, EchoStar and other leases were not renewed, and three U.S. carriers supply 66.5% of revenue, so a further carrier event would reach cash flow quickly.

fields.value: Leverage is high and has not fallen through debt reduction. Net debt was 6.45x adjusted EBITDA and 7.39x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 6.61x and 7.73x at the end of 2025, and debt principal ended the nine months USD 15.25 million higher; counting the escrow held for the January 2025 repayment, end-2024 adjusted leverage was 6.46x, so leverage has been roughly flat near 6.5x for two years. Pro forma for the purchase of 69 sites expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, with no day stated, net leverage is 7.40x on reported EBITDA; the pro forma figure on adjusted EBITDA, for the dividend payable on 2026-12-10 and for the Peru sale is not established.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for contractual maturities but depends on market access for the anticipated dates. A tranche not repaid on its date traps cash flow from its towers and steps its interest up by at least 5 percentage points, so the dates behave like maturities for planning even though the legal maturities are decades away.

No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, but management ranks acquisitions and new towers, then buybacks, then dividend growth, and the nine-month record put payouts ahead of debt reduction; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium. The debt the filings state as secured fell to 49.90% of principal from 76.85% at the 2025 year end and sits in a non-recourse pool covering 19.01% of towers; reported covenant ratios and the pool's coverage ratio are not printed, so headroom is not established.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate-but-refinancing-dependent view is that the contractual picture is comfortable and the payouts are discretionary. Only the USD 1,500 million 2020 Senior Notes have a final maturity inside twelve months, and liquidity covers that 194.50%; the company states that cash, facility availability and operating cash flow will cover debt service and final maturities over the next twelve months; it sold USD 3,500 million of unsecured notes in July 2026 and repaid earlier Tower Securities on or within days of their anticipated dates; and ending buybacks alone would free cash flow equal to the dividend.

It would weaken if the date passes unrefinanced, if buybacks are funded by revolver or commercial paper borrowings, if domestic churn runs above the guided range, or if the unseen debt documents show covenant ceilings or restricted-payment capacity tighter than the filings imply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strengths, in rank order, are these. The contracted, high-margin site leasing base is first: it produced 98.3% of segment operating profit, with margins of 84.24% in the U.S. and 70.42% abroad, and its recurring rent covers fixed charges and keeps cash interest at 24.60% of adjusted EBITDA. Demonstrated capital-markets access is second: USD 3,500 million of unsecured notes in July 2026, an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver and a commercial paper program give refinancing a path that does not depend on the securitisation market alone. Third is a fixed-rate, laddered debt stack with a low weighted average coupon of 3.94%, which holds near-term interest cost down until the older tranches reset. Fourth is control of the land: about 71% of towers sit on owned, perpetual or long-dated land interests with a 35-year average remaining life. Fifth is discretion: no sponsor is identified and the board can cut buybacks, which are about the size of the dividend, at its sole discretion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaknesses, in rank order, are these. Leverage comes first: net debt is 6.45x adjusted EBITDA and 7.39x reported EBITDA (7.40x on reported EBITDA pro forma for the 69-site purchase; other post-balance-sheet effects not established) with principal flat, so creditors carry the same leverage as two years ago. Second, payouts absorb 98.49% of free cash flow, leaving nothing for debt reduction. Third, the near-term maturity concentration: USD 3,560 million of principal falls at anticipated dates within twelve months against liquidity that covers 81.95%. Fourth, customer concentration and churn: three carriers supply 66.5% of revenue, EchoStar has defaulted, and guided 2026 churn is about 6.61% to 6.81% of FY2025 site leasing revenue. Fifth, the interest reset against flat earnings: adjusted EBITDA was flat at constant currency in nine months 2026 and fell in the third quarter while cover on run-rate coupons is 3.78x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SBA owns and operates 45,252 wireless towers at 2026-09-30, in the United States, Brazil, Central America and Africa, and leases antenna space to carriers under long contracts; it has built towers for carriers since 1989 and owned them since 1997. Site leasing is 98.3% of segment operating profit and site development, a U.S. project business, is 6.90% of nine-month 2026 revenue. Tenant leases run 5 to 10 years in the U.S. and 5 to 15 years abroad with renewal options held by the tenant, so revenue is highly visible, while the business has grown through acquisitions, notably the Millicom purchase in Central America, and has exited five countries since the start of 2025. The model supports debt service because rent is contracted and escalating, but it is concentrated in three U.S. carriers and exposed to non-renewal when carriers consolidate, which is the source of the current churn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registrant is a Florida holding company whose only significant asset is 100% of SBA Telecommunications, LLC; it is a REIT, has one class of common stock outstanding, and no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, with the articles generally capping any holder at 9.8%. Cash to the parent comes only from subsidiary distributions, and the Tower Securities borrowers sit in a separate non-recourse pool that may not borrow elsewhere, so in our reading cash in that pool is structurally ahead of parent-level creditors until released. The July 2026 notes and revolver are obligations of the registrant and are unsecured, but their guarantors and ranking are not stated. The credit implication is that parent notes rely on distributions from subsidiaries and on the release of pool cash, which a missed anticipated date would interrupt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, pages 46 and 52; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring, escalating and concentrated rather than cyclical. Domestic revenue grows only through escalators, new leases and amendments, and is offset by non-renewals; domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.14% in nine months 2026 while total revenue rose 1.77% because international site leasing grew 24.81% on reported figures and 18.5% at constant currency. Pricing power is limited: the annual report says competition has pushed it into master lease agreements with discounts and term concessions, and the three U.S. carriers hold the buyer power. Management guides 2026 churn at USD 133.0 million to USD 136.0 million in the U.S. and USD 37.0 million to USD 39.0 million abroad, which is 6.61% to 6.81% of FY2025 site leasing revenue; the credit implication is that new leases and escalators must outrun churn of that size for revenue to grow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sbac.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C2; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly fixed per tower: cost of revenue is primarily ground lease rent, and management says operating costs for owned towers do not generally rise when tenants are added, so lost tenants remove high-margin revenue while costs stay. The domestic segment margin eased to 84.24% from 85.16% in nine months 2025 and the international margin rose to 70.42% from 69.53%, helped by the ground lease purchase program, and the company-wide adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue fell to 67.78% from 70.69% in FY2024, partly because lower-margin site development grew in FY2025 and domestic rent fell. Inflation is partly passed through, since the South American and African leases are index-linked, but only 12.6% of international leases have fixed escalators, so the real risk is in markets where inflation exceeds fixed rates. Margins can be defended against modest churn but operating leverage works against the issuer if domestic revenue keeps falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low for the business and largely discretionary. Maintenance and general corporate spending is guided at USD 61.0 million to USD 65.0 million for 2026, against discretionary spending of USD 480.0 million to USD 490.0 million that covers acquisitions, new builds, augmentations and ground lease purchases; capital expenditure was 12.74% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA. Cash interest takes 24.60% and cash taxes USD 99.490 million over the same period, leaving operating cash flow after capital expenditure at 54.40% of adjusted EBITDA. That conversion is durable because the largest uses, buybacks and growth spending, can be cut, but it already funds a dividend of 49.19% of free cash flow, so little is left for debt reduction unless buybacks stop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate: the company competes with large independent tower companies, regional owners and carriers' own towers, and says pricing pressure has produced master lease agreements with discounts and term concessions; the credit effect is slower rent growth and some non-renewals rather than a threat to existing contracts. The threat of new entrants is moderate to low because towers need zoning approval, land control and capital, although the annual report warns that competitors building near existing towers can draw tenants away. The threat of substitutes is a longer-dated risk, since small cells, distributed antenna systems and low-earth-orbit satellite could reduce macro tower demand, though the annual report gives no sign that it has yet. Buyer power is high because three national carriers account for 66.5% of revenue and can consolidate or share networks, as the Sprint and EchoStar churn shows, and this is the force that most affects cash flow. Supplier power is moderate: landowners can refuse renewal or sell to aggregators, but about 71% of towers sit on owned or long-dated land with an average remaining life of 35 years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and regulatory factors change the credit conclusion and are covered; social and political factors are secondary. Interest rates matter twice, because higher rates raise the cost of refinancing the low-coupon maturities and reduce the capital carriers can spend on networks, and a 1% rise in variable rates would lift nine-month interest expense by about 1.9%. Currency matters in Brazil, where a 10% fall in the real cuts revenue by 1.2%, and in a USD 863.7 million book of intercompany loans that is remeasured through income. Regulation matters through FCC and FAA tower rules and local zoning, which slow new builds, and through a Brazilian tax dispute with a reasonably possible loss range of up to USD 115.5 million before USD 201.0 million of penalties and interest, which the company has not accrued. The credit consequence is a modest, mostly manageable drag, with refinancing cost the largest macro channel.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are contracted high-margin rent, demonstrated bond-market access, a fixed-rate laddered debt stack and long-dated land control. Weaknesses are leverage near 6.5x adjusted EBITDA, payouts that absorb nearly all free cash flow, customer concentration and a near-term maturity cluster. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a decision to redirect buybacks to debt reduction, which would cut payouts to the dividend alone, spectrum deployment that adds tenants to existing towers, and tower-based data centre or edge services the company is exploring. Threats are further carrier consolidation or failure, an unrefinanced anticipated repayment date that traps cash flow, interest cost resets on the older tranches and currency weakness in Brazil.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are scale and market position in contracted tower rent, high and stable segment margins, long land tenure and open bond-market access. The main constraints are leverage near 6.5x adjusted EBITDA, 98.49% of free cash flow paid out, a maturity cluster at anticipated dates and customer concentration. The trend is flat to slightly weaker: adjusted leverage fell from 7.07x at the end of 2024 mainly because USD 1,165 million of escrow cash was classified as restricted, cover on adjusted EBITDA slipped from 4.79x to 4.07x, and EBITDA growth stalled at constant currency. Key missing datapoints are the outcome of the 2026-11-09 date, covenant ratios, the pool's coverage ratio, ratings and market pricing. The financial profile is therefore adequate with a negative bias on interest cover and a positive offset in market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the outlook is stable operating results with rising interest cost. Management expects core leasing revenue to grow on a currency-neutral basis despite elevated churn, with discretionary spending of USD 480.0 million to USD 490.0 million in 2026, while USD 3,560 million of principal reaches anticipated dates by April 2027 and the older tranches reset toward the July 2026 coupons, which would take cover on adjusted EBITDA to about 3.22x. Over three to five years the maturities at principal are USD 1,450 million in 2028, USD 2,950 million in 2029 and USD 1,350 million in 2030, with USD 3,045 million after that, so 2027 is the largest date and 2029 the next. Tailwinds are carrier spectrum deployment and growing mobile data traffic, which the annual report cites, and international tenancy growth; headwinds are carrier consolidation, the EchoStar default and spectrum sale, higher rates for carriers and for the issuer, and substitute architectures. The net credit effect is neutral on revenue and negative on interest cost, so deleveraging has to come from payout restraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most realistic downside combines a closed secured-debt window with another year of domestic churn. The initiating condition is that the 2021-1C Tower Securities are not refinanced on 2026-11-09 and the market stays shut into the first half of 2027; the first operational break is the passed date, which traps excess cash flow from the pool's towers and adds at least 5 percentage points to the tranche's rate, or at least USD 58.25 million a year. The company's remedy, used in January 2026 for the 2020-1C Tower Securities, is a revolver draw, which at the revolver's rate of 4.913% costs USD 57.24 million a year against USD 19.00 million at the tranche's coupon and uses USD 1,165 million of the USD 2,500 million facility. Then the 2020 Senior Notes fall due on 2027-02-15 and the 2021-2C Tower Securities on 2027-04-09; with buybacks stopped, resources to 2027-04-09 are USD 2,917.532 million plus about USD 279.678 million of free cash flow after dividends, leaving a shortfall of about USD 362.790 million against the USD 3,560 million due. If churn repeats at the top of the guided range, adjusted EBITDA falls by about USD 142.030 million to about USD 1,791.276 million, net leverage on adjusted EBITDA rises to 6.97x (pro forma adjustments for the post-balance-sheet events are not established on that basis), cover on run-rate coupons with the reset falls to 2.99x, and free cash flow after dividends falls to about USD 267.960 million. Stopping buybacks is already assumed in the shortfall, so the gap would have to be met by pausing discretionary spending (USD 251.178 million to USD 256.411 million pro rata to 2027-04-09), a smaller dividend, asset sale proceeds or new issuance. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through April 2027, but only with market access or a pause in growth spending and shareholder returns; default risk is not evidenced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Sba Communications Corp presents a strong business profile supported by contracted, high-margin tower rent, long land tenure and demonstrated bond-market access, but credit quality is constrained by leverage near 6.5x adjusted EBITDA, payouts that absorb nearly all free cash flow and a maturity cluster at anticipated dates. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because rent is recurring and buybacks are discretionary, although domestic churn and flat adjusted EBITDA at constant currency limit growth. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the outcome of the 2021-1C date, the willingness of the secured market and the bond market to take the 2027 tranches at coupons well above the legacy ones, and on whether the board redirects buybacks to debt reduction. The primary downside path is a missed anticipated date during a closed market combined with another year of churn, which would compress cover below 3.0x. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant ratios, the pool's coverage ratio, ratings, market pricing and filings after 2026-11-05. Top risk: refinancing of the 2026 and 2027 maturities at much higher coupons while payouts continue.
